key_insight: Induction thermography detected micrometre-scale cracks in WC-10Co-4Cr coatings, with minimum resolved widths of approximately 1 µm on ground surfaces and 1.7 µm on as-sprayed surfaces.
engineering_relevance: Non-destructive crack inspection could improve maintenance and product quality in coated calender rollers, where micrometre-scale dimensional precision is critical.
method: Tested WC-10Co-4Cr-coated C60 steel with ground and as-sprayed surfaces.
Induced cracks using mechanical strains of 0.12–0.4% and thermal shock.
Evaluated induction thermography signals using Fourier analysis and principal component analysis.
evidence_signal: Tests covered crack widths of approximately 1–4.5 µm and depths up to the full coating thickness of approximately 400 µm; both dimensions influenced thermal contrast, with deeper cracks producing stronger signals.
watch_item: Detection sensitivity depends on surface condition and crack geometry, so the reported minimum resolved widths should not be treated as universal inspection limits.
paper_title: Evaluation of Induction Thermography for the Detection of Cracks Due to Mechanical and Thermal Stress in WC-10Co-4Cr Coatings
